messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing follow-up — token volumes & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our call:

- Observed flows: onboarding flows + 3 feature endpoints (summarization, personalization prompting, document Q&A).
- Your rough monthly token estimate: 150M — 250M tokens/month initially, with seasonal spikes up to ~400M in Q4.
- Target budget range you mentioned: $8k — $20k / month for inference (pilot to early production) depending on SLA and throughput.

I promised a quant-focused follow-up on the unit economics and a target $/1M tokens baseline so you can map to feature-level P&L. Attached is a quick model and pricing matrix. High-level starters I recommend we evaluate:

1) Target list price band: $35 — $120 per 1M tokens depending on latency, quantization, and batch assumptions (hosted vs dedicated).
2) Pilot recommendation: commit to a 3-month trial at a higher per-token rate but with caps and credits so you can validate quality & latency.
3) Unit economics we’ll map: $/feature (inference-only), incremental feature margin, CAC payback using forecasted MRR, and sensitivity to quantization (int8 vs fp16).

Action items:
- Sarah: confirm whether the 150–250M estimate includes embeddings (yes/no) and which features are priority for pilot.
- Tom: share any procurement constraints / target PO timeline.
- Marissa (me): will send an itemized $/1M tokens break-down and a simple feature-level P&L you can drop into your financial model.

Attachments: unit_econ_model.xlsx (working model), pricing_matrix.pdf (hosted vs dedicated).

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole

Sarah —

Attached are two items: a compact working model (unit_econ_model.xlsx) and a short pricing matrix PDF that sketches three realistic price points and assumptions. Summary below (conservative / baseline / aggressive):

- Hosted (no commit): $120 / 1M tokens (low-latency, premium)  | Baseline: $75 / 1M | Aggressive (volume discount): $45 / 1M
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 3–12 month commit): $55 / 1M | Baseline: $35 / 1M | Aggressive: $25 / 1M

Notes and assumptions (short):
- Token definition: generation tokens only; embeddings priced separately.
- Latency: hosted tiers assume 95th pctl < 300ms; dedicated pricing assumes production SLOs with fixed throughput.
- Quantization: moving from fp16 -> int8 reduces per-token infra by ~25–35% in our model.
- Batching & KV cache: effective per-token cost can drop further for repeated prefixes; model includes a conservative 10% optimization for common flows.

Feature-level example (monthly inference-only cost at 250M tokens split):
- Document Q&A (60% of gen tokens = 150M): dedicated baseline $35/1M => $5,250/month
- Summarization (30% = 75M): dedicated baseline $35/1M => $2,625/month
- Personalization prompts (10% = 25M): dedicated baseline $35/1M => $875/month
- Total inference-only: $8,750/month (dedicated baseline)

CAC payback examples (assumptions):
- If ARPU per new customer feature set = $3,000 MRR and gross margin target before inference = 70%
- Incremental gross margin after inference cost (using the $8,750 estimate) => monthly incremental margin delta = 3,000 * 0.7 - (8,750 / N_customers).
- For pilot-to-paid with ~10 customers in initial cohort, inference per-customer = $875/month, incremental margin per customer ~ (2,100 - 875) = $1,225. At $1,225/month contribution, CAC payback of a $9,000 CAC is ~7.3 months (within your <9 month target).

I included the model with adjustable levers (token mix, price per 1M, quantization savings, batch gains) so you can run scenarios.

Next steps:
- Sarah: confirm whether you want us to model a 6- or 12-month committed reserved plan vs a pay-as-you-go pilot.
- Tom: if procurement is OK with a 90-day pilot at the dedicated baseline price, we'll prepare a scoped MSA + SOW (I can loop legal once procurement signals).
- I'll loop in Rishi (cc) for discount approvals should you ask for a blended committed rate.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Internal — FintechX pricing request & discount/commit ask

Team — quick internal note and ask. FintechX (Sarah/Tom) confirmed token mix and priority features; budget-bound pilot $8k–$20k/mo. My recommended commercial approach:

- Offer a 90-day pilot scoped to their priority features at a dedicated baseline price of $35 / 1M tokens, with up to 250M gen tokens covered by the pilot and a $5k credit if we miss SLA on 95th pct latency.
- Provide optional 6- or 12-month reserved capacity pricing for production: 6mo commit at $30 / 1M; 12mo commit at $25 / 1M (both assume a minimum monthly committed spend aligning with expected 250–400M volumes).
- If they ask for blending/compression to land in $8k–$12k pilot spend, propose a 10% discount on baseline + a short-term feature credit rather than lowering the per-token list materially. Keeps unit economics intact.

Attached model shows resulting unit economics and CAC payback scenarios. Key internal asks:
1) Approval to offer a pilot at $35/1M with the SLA credit described.
2) Approval to offer up to a 10% one-time discount for pilot sign (sales-led credit) or a longer-term blended discount subject to procurement PO.

Quick numbers (for Rishi/Finance review):
- Pilot inference-only cost at 250M (dedicated baseline): $8,750/month.
- If we give 10% discount => $7,875/month. Difference to Redwood margin (assume infra blended cost ~$18/1M tokens at this commit) => margin still healthy (>40%).
- CAC payback: at 10-customer cohort example in the external note, payback ~7.3 months. With discount still within target.

Please reply-all with approval or changes; if approved, I'll share the SOW template with procurement and prep legal.

Thanks —
Marissa
